items.title: Schema in the AI Era: From Rich Results to Machine Interpretation
items.summary: Schema is shifting from "nice-to-have for rich results" to "interpretation infrastructure" that reduces ambiguity for machines. This session delved into schema graphs, template-first rollouts, and the QA needs that are boring but necessary. The focus of this presentation was pragmatic: which schema work tends to pay off, how to operationalise it across large sites, and how to communicate it internally as data engineering—worthy of investment.To stay focused on things that make a business impact, this session will deliver a prioritised schema roadmap (templates first; highest-intent entities) to help attendees, a QA and governance process to prevent silent schema failures, and help for those in-house (or even for agencies) to create an internal business case framing schema as infrastructure for discovery. All in 20 minutes so as can be imagined, there are a lot of slides which deliver detailed summaries of the points without excess of bullet points which get tedious or boring essays on slides. It does make this deck more compact but each slide is packed with delicious details.LLM do not 'understand' schema, they do not encode schema elements within their databases, schema does not play a direct part in relating tokens within vectors. To better understand how transformers work, and how they store and retrieve information, I recommend 3 Blue 1 Brown and his series of videos on Deep Learning. All his videos are fantastic, making mathematics accessible and explaining how LLMs work and therefore why Schema is best for RAG.

items.title: The Hidden Architecture of High-Ranking eCommerce Product Pages: The Technical Systems That Actually Move Revenue
items.summary: Slides from my BrightonSEO talk on the technical systems behind ecommerce product pages.I trace one product across its URL and canonical, rendered page, Product markup, Merchant Centre feed and internal links, showing where product facts can disagree and how to investigate those contradictions.Using an anonymised client case study and practical variant examples, I explain how to choose a variant model and turn findings into developer tickets with clear QA checks. A walkthrough that SEOs and ecommerce teams can apply to their own catalogue.
